items.note: In the black footer the email field gets a 2px danger border, and below it sits a red-dot icon with a one-line message in primary text; the pink submit stays beside it. This is the spec's inline error recipe: a person sees at once what went wrong and how to fix it. It keeps the ink-hairline character of the reference's form screen (07).

The error itself is the same as in light: a white field with a danger border, a dot icon and the message, and it reads clearly. The page around it is a grey ground with pure-black cards, the reverse of the reference's dark mode (11), where the ground is black and the boxes are a step lighter.

The stacked footer form keeps the 2px danger field, the pink submit beside it and the dot icon with its message under it, all within the phone width. It stays as plain and drawn as the reference's phone app screen (10).

The form becomes a white ink panel with a static hard shadow, a status dot and a one-line confirmation, next to a teal die-cut word badge holding an outlined lemon word ('sent'/'thanks'/'done'). This follows the spec's toast and success-badge recipe and has the reference's sticker cheer. The badge's ink slab disappears into the black footer.

The word badge is kept, but in two samples the confirmation panel is pure black on the black footer, held only by a faint hairline, so it no longer reads as a lifted white slip. The grey-ground, black-card reversal against the reference's dark mode (11) also runs through the page.
On the phone, the white confirmation panel with its hard shadow and the teal word badge stack in the footer, and nothing overlaps. Clear and in the reference's language.

Under the focused search field (ink border with a pink halo) sits a dashed white box. It holds a drawn paper-slip sticker with a curled end and ruled lines, one sentence, a hint, and a black or outline clear action. This is the reference's dashed empty state (06), raised with a drawn object. The slip is small and uncoloured.

Same structure, but the dashed box becomes a black panel on the grey ground, and in one sample the dash is barely visible. The white slip sticker carries the state; it reads clearly, but the reversed dark tones make it flatter than the reference's dark mode.

Full-width dashed box with the slip sticker, the sentence and the clear action under the halo-focused field. It matches the reference's phone empty state (10) closely, with a drawn object instead of the small glyph.
The focused current-nav pill (black) gets a 2px ink ring at a 2px offset that follows the pill shape. This is a crisp, drawn focus like the reference's focus-visible capture, with no glow.
In dark mode the current pill turns white and the focus ring turns white with an offset, as the reference swaps its nav pill (11). The ring is clearly visible on the black header.
Focus lands on the two-line menu button (or the header link) with a 2px ink ring that is easy to see. The header stays a single tidy row, as in the reference's phone header.

The hero objects (mug, curled slip, notebook, envelope, pencil, bookmark) are flat band-colour fills with even ink outlines, cropped at the band edges. They are mostly thin line drawings of 100–150px, with little extruded thickness. One sample has a single small marker in a short band, and another repeats the pencil. The reference's coins are 200px die-cut objects with deep rims that dominate the corners.

In all three samples the article image is a generic sun-and-mountains placeholder glyph, on grey in two of them and on periwinkle in one. It is not a drawing of the article's subject and does not follow the sticker or vignette recipe. The reference keeps empty media white and dashed, or draws a real object.
The same sun-and-mountains glyph as the other article, identical in every sample, so two different subjects share one stock picture. Nothing of the reference's distinct, chunky, ink-drawn objects.

One small header-band sticker per sample (a mug, a notebook with a spine slab, an envelope) on the periwinkle band. Each is cleanly drawn and its own object, but at about 70px it is small and mostly flat next to the reference's stickers.

The only animations are the hero and header stickers on the linear scroll-linked ft-drift; nothing loops, fades or enters on load. This is the sparse, paper-like motion the spec describes, without the marquee the reference uses on marketing pages.

findings.summary: Article images are one generic sun-and-mountains placeholder glyph, repeated across different articles and across all samples, on grey or a flat band fill. They are not drawings of the article's subject. The reference never shows stock picture glyphs: empty media is a white dashed box, and every drawing is a distinct, chunky, ink-outlined object.
findings.promptFix: When content has no image of its own (an article cover, a product photo, an avatar), never draw a generic picture glyph (sun and mountains, a landscape, a photo icon). Either draw that item's own subject as a circle vignette in the sticker recipe (band-colour ground, 2–4 flat ink-outlined objects named by the item's topic, distinct per item), or show a white box with a 1px dashed ink border and a small solid ink glyph of the item's type. No grey fills.

findings.summary: Hero stickers are still thinner, smaller and flatter than the reference's. Most are 100–150px line drawings with no extruded side or back face. One sample puts a single small marker in a short header-style band instead of 4–6 objects ringing the headline, and another uses the same pencil twice. The reference's 200px die-cut coins with deep rims dominate the band corners.
findings.promptFix: A landing or home hero is a full hero band (marketing block padding, hero-size headline), never a compact header band, and rings the headline with 4–6 different stickers, no object drawn twice. Each sticker is 160–240px wide on desktop and shows its thickness: a back face or side band at least 8% of the object's height, in the same fill and outlined in ink, plus 1–3 inner strokes. A single flat outline is not a sticker.

findings.summary: Dark mode still reverses the reference's depth: the page ground is dark grey and the cards, empty box and confirmation panel are pure black, so the confirmation slip disappears into the black footer and dashed boxes lose their edge. The reference uses a black ground with boxes a step lighter.
findings.promptFix: Dark mode: the page ground (`color.surface.default`) is black (#000000), and raised boxes (`color.surface.raised`) are one step lighter (#242423), edged with the 35% white hairline; a toast or panel shown on the black footer stays on the raised tone so it reads as lifted.
